messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 03:42 UTC — Elevated 4xx/5xx rate detected on /v1/stream (us-east-1). Signature: client_frame_decode_error. Affected hosts: 12. Auto-created incident thread.

maria: seeing a big spike in paging errors right after the v5 client canary (v5.0.2) started rolling at ~03:14 UTC. Logs show frame decode failures and many clients stuck in connect/retry. Can reproduce quickly with a v5 binary + long-paging request.

jon: pinging oncall, this looks like a client->server protocol mismatch. @oncall-amber are you able to grab the gateway logs and the canary deployment details?

oncall-amber: looking now. grabbing recent deploys...

deploy-bot: Deploy event: deploy_id=deploy-2026-03-15-0312, artifact=sdk-server:v2.8.1, started_by=ci/cd, canary=10% traffic to hosts (ip-range x.x.x.x).

oncall-amber: gateway logs show repeated errors: `client_frame_decode_error: invalid_magic=0x0f` from connections where user-agent contains `redwood-sdk-v5`. Non-v5 traffic looks ok so far.

pradeep: this smells like a streaming protocol field reordering in v5 client. v5 changed the frame header order in one commit — server should be backward-compatible but apparently not. Recommend immediate kill-switch of new client acceptance (FF kill) or revert canary.

maria: agreed — impact: some customers report stalled streaming responses during paging. Not all requests fail, but enough to trigger user-visible degraded UX. Support has a couple of priority customers on the list.

support-lead: list of impacted customers from error logs: AcmeCorp (high), SatoriDocs (med), beta-internal (low). Support is drafting customer messages. No data loss reported, just timeouts and retries.

jon: mitigation options: 1) rollback server to previous artifact (but server is probably fine), 2) flip feature flag to reject v5 handshake, or 3) push client hotfix. Fastest is to flip FF so gateways treat v5 UA as incompatible and route to legacy handshake.

oncall-amber: where is the client-compat kill flag in the FF service?

pradeep: it's `ff.client_handshake.v5_compat` with values `enabled|disabled`. Default is enabled. Set to disabled to force legacy codepath.

maria: can someone verify the read path for the flag won't affect other features?

ops-sre: `ff.client_handshake.v5_compat` only gated at handshake parser. Changing it flips the parser codepath; downstream state unaffected. Quick test on staging looks fine.

maria: ok do it. We need to do it ASAP and monitor for reduction in error rate.

deploy-bot: FF toggle command (internal):
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $FF_ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"flag":"ff.client_handshake.v5_compat","value":"disabled","reason":"emergency: client v5 streaming protocol mismatch"}' \
  https://featureflags.internal.redwood/api/v1/toggle
```

oncall-amber: flipping now.

oncall-amber: ✅ flip complete. `ff.client_handshake.v5_compat` = disabled across us-east-1 (propagated to edge routers).

incident-bot: [STATUS] 03:55 UTC — Error rate decreased by ~78% over 3 minutes after FF flip. Current error rate trending down.

kevin: confirmed on dashboards — 4xx spikes normalized. Some sporadic timeouts remain but far lower. Good catch.

maria: creating incident SEV-2 and assigning owners. Immediate actions: (a) keep FF off, (b) pause v5 client rollout, (c) prepare server-side compatible patch and client-side patch.

pm-elaine: noted. I'll pause the release pipeline for v5 across regions and notify the release manager.

support-lead: sending customer comms now. Draft to AcmeCorp: "We're aware of streaming degradation affecting paging; we applied an emergency compatibility change and paused the rollout. No data lost. We'll follow up with ETA for full restore." :thumbsup:

maria: handoff — @jon you'll take primary exec updates, @pradeep you own mitigation engineering, @oncall-amber continue monitoring for next hour, support-lead owns customer comms.

jon: acknowledged. I'll ping legal/comms if customers escalate.

pradeep: root cause triage plan: 1) reproduce minimal failing handshake, 2) diff v4/v5 client frame headers, 3) check server parser for non-symmetric field handling, 4) write regression tests and add to gate.

ops-sre: capturing traffic dump for failed handshake flows and saving to s3://redwood-incidents/2419803333/ for postmortem.

maria: docs-bot please create incident doc skeleton.

docs-bot: Incident doc created: https://internal.redwood/incidents/2419803333 — owner=@pradeep, severity=SEV-2.

support-lead: once we have root cause and ETA we'll follow up with customers. Any timeline guesses?

pradeep: quick estimate: server patch + canary (2-3 hours) if it's a simple parse bug. If deeper protocol assumption, might be longer. We'll prioritize.

jon: reminder: if error rate increases after we re-enable FF, we should revert immediately or re-enable old behavior. Keep rollback path rehearsed.

maria: agreed. For now we keep FF disabled and pause client rollout globally. We'll update thread with timeline changes.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] 04:20 UTC — Monitoring continues. Current error rate stable and within baseline for non-v5 traffic. Next update in 30m or on major change.

oncall-amber: handing off to night oncall @ops-sre in 25m — I'll leave monitoring dashboard open and escalate if anything flares.

ops-sre: taking handoff. I'll watch the alerts and maintain the FF state until engineering says otherwise.

maria: thanks team. Postmortem owner @pradeep. We'll fill in timeline, root cause, mitigations, and action items (add regression test, add FF automated rollback on error spike, add UA parsing contract tests).

jon: I'll draft the external post-incident note once we have RCA.

incident-bot: [CLOSEABLE] 06:14 UTC — Error rates stable. Action items assigned. Mark incident for postmortem.

maria: closing thread for now, will reopen if anything changes. :white_check_mark:
